findings.title: [P1] Reject cross-tenant document reads
findings.body: When `userTenant !== documentTenant`, `canReadDocument` now returns `true` unconditionally. Any authorization flow relying on this function can therefore expose one tenant’s documents to users from another tenant. Preserve the tenant comparison or apply an equivalent access check.

findings.title: [P1] Restore tenant isolation for document reads
findings.body:
`canReadDocument("tenant-a", "tenant-b")` now returns `true`, allowing any caller relying on this authorization check to grant cross-tenant document access.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Preserve the exported document label contract
findings.body:
Consumers expecting the exported value or inferred literal type `"Document"` now receive `"Document record"`, breaking exact-value assertions, serialization/mapping logic, and TypeScript assignments constrained to the previous literal.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Reject cross-tenant document reads
findings.body:
`canReadDocument` now grants access unconditionally. Any request where `userTenant !== documentTenant` bypasses tenant isolation and can expose another tenant’s documents to an unauthorized user.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
